questions.stem:
With respect to a fixed origin $O$, the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ are given by the equations
$$l_1: \mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\4\\-5\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\6\end{pmatrix} \qquad l_2: \mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}13\\-1\\4\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}5\\1\\-3\end{pmatrix}$$
where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalar parameters.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $l_1$ and $l_2$ meet and find the position vector of their point of intersection $A$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: For writing down any 2 of these equations: $4+2\lambda=13+5\mu$, $4-3\lambda=-1+\mu$, $-5+6\lambda=4-3\mu$
M1: Full method for finding $\lambda$ or $\mu$
A1: Both correct values $\lambda=2$, $\mu=-1$
B1: Shows that the parameters satisfy the third equation and makes a conclusion: $-5+6\lambda=-5+12=7$, $4-3\mu=4+3=7$, So lines intersect
M1: Uses their $\lambda$ or $\mu$ to find $A$: $\lambda=2\to(4+4)\mathbf{i}+(4-6)\mathbf{j}+(-5+12)\mathbf{k}$ or $\mu=-1\to(13-5)\mathbf{i}+(-1-1)\mathbf{j}+(4+3)\mathbf{k}$
A1: Correct vector or coordinates $8\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- E.g. $4+2\lambda=13+5\mu$, $4-3\lambda=-1+\mu$ $\Rightarrow\lambda=...$ or $\mu=...$ M1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the acute angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$, giving your answer in degrees to one decimal place.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Full attempt at the scalar product between the direction vectors: $\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\6\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}5\\1\\-3\end{pmatrix}=10-3-18=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}\sqrt{5^2+1^2+3^2}\cos\theta$
A1: Correct magnitude for $\cos\theta$ (may be implied by e.g. $\theta=105.4...$ or $74.6...$): $\cos\theta=\pm\frac{11}{7\sqrt{35}}$
A1: Awrt 74.6 $\theta=74.6°$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A circle with centre $A$ and radius 35 cuts the line $l_1$ at the points $P$ and $Q$.
Given that the $x$ coordinate of $P$ is greater than the $x$ coordinate of $Q$,
(c) find the coordinates of $P$ and the coordinates of $Q$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Finds the magnitude of the direction of $l_1$: $|2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{k}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}=7$
M1: Correct strategy for one of the points: $35\div7=5\Rightarrow \lambda=5$, $8\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}\pm5(2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{k})$
A1: One correct point (ignore labels) $(18,-17,37)$ or $(-2,13,-23)$
A1: Correct points with correct labels $P(18,-17,37)$ and $Q(-2,13,-23)$
